First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-6t-10)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-10t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(5)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(5)^{3}-3(5)^{2}-10(5)+C \\ 0 & =125-75-50+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the runner at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-10t.$

To find the time interval in which the runner is moving to the *left*, we must solve the inequality $v<0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-10t=t(t-5)(t+2)<0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094076/assets/0e6c4aca5cba41c90fb369f0b6d820f15709f0b6b28f9b4c9c3fefea9cc906dc.png)

From the graph, we see that $v<0$ whenever $0\,<\,t\,<\,5.$
